content.title: Recommendations for diagnosis of pulmonary embolism (PE)

recommendations.text: In suspected high-risk PE with haemodynamic instability, bedside echocardiography or emergency CTPA (depending on availability and clinical circumstances) is recommended for diagnosis.
Initiation of i.v. anticoagulation with unfractionated heparin (UFH), including a weight‑adjusted bolus injection, is recommended without delay in patients with suspected high-risk PE.
Use of validated criteria for diagnosis of PE is recommended.
Initiation of anticoagulation is recommended without delay in patients with high or intermediate clinical probability of PE while diagnostic workup is in progress.
Diagnostic strategy should be based on clinical probability, assessed by clinical judgment or a validated prediction rule.

Plasma D-dimer measurement, using a highly sensitive assay, is recommended in outpatients/emergency department patients with low or intermediate clinical probability, or those who are PE-unlikely, to reduce unnecessary imaging and irradiation.

As an alternative to a fixed D-dimer cut-off, a negative D-dimer test using an age-adjusted cut-off (age × 10 µg/L for patients >50 years) should be considered to exclude PE in patients with low or intermediate clinical probability.
D-dimer measurement is not recommended in patients with high clinical probability, as a normal result does not safely exclude PE when using a highly sensitive assay.
Reject the diagnosis of PE (without further testing) if CTPA is normal in a patient with low or intermediate clinical probability, or who is PE-unlikely.
Accept the diagnosis of PE (without further testing) if CTPA shows a segmental or more proximal filling defect in a patient with intermediate or high clinical probability.
If CTPA is normal in a patient with high clinical probability, further testing should be considered (CTPA alone may not be sufficient).
CT venography is not recommended as an adjunct to CTPA.
Reject the diagnosis of PE (without further testing) if the perfusion lung scan is normal.
Consider accepting the diagnosis of PE (without further testing) if the V/Q scan yields high probability for PE.
A non-diagnostic V/Q scan combined with a negative proximal compression ultrasonography (CUS) may be considered to exclude PE in patients with low clinical probability or who are PE-unlikely.
V/Q SPECT may be considered for PE diagnosis.
Accept the diagnosis of VTE (and PE) if CUS shows a proximal DVT in a patient with clinical suspicion of PE.
If CUS shows only a distal DVT, further testing should be considered to confirm PE.
If a positive proximal CUS is used to confirm PE, assessment of PE severity should be considered to permit risk-adjusted management.
MRA is not recommended for ruling out PE.

sections.heading: Abbreviations (selected)
sections.notes: CT = computed tomographic; CTPA = computed tomography pulmonary angiography; CUS = compression ultrasonography; DVT = deep vein thrombosis; i.v. = intravenous; MRA = magnetic resonance angiography; PE = pulmonary embolism; SPECT = single-photon emission computed tomography; UFH = unfractionated heparin; V/Q = ventilation/perfusion; VTE = venous thromboembolism.

sections.notes: a = Class of recommendation. b = Level of evidence.
